risk.rationale: Cache authority, invalidation correctness, commit-bound evidence rematerialization, public report and error schemas, snapshot equivalence, and atomic head publication

approved: S4 RepositorySnapshotV4, ExtractionChunkV2, KnowledgeGraphV2, DocumentationManifestV1, docs, and exact query contracts
must_remain_byte_compatible: every file bound by the accepted S4 contract bundle

expected_red.precondition: This governance package and a separate policy binding are merged, then the black-box acceptance harness is added before production implementation.
expected_red.expected_failure: The current local runtime can create the S4 baseline, but the refresh command is not yet recognized; the exact invocation returns ErrorV2 input.invalid_revision, emits no report, creates no store, and publishes no target head.
rejected_failures: Git, Cargo, rustc, build, target, hook, plugin, network, model, or Council execution
two cold scans mislabeled as incremental reuse
baseline public chunk bytes copied with stale commit evidence
changed-source evidence retaining the baseline blob or span
expected_red.reason_not_run: The original governance package preceded protected requirement and policy binding; the corrected bootstrap observation is executed only by the first implementation issue.

hit_requires: exact repository, ownership, path, blob, and version fields

report.set_order: UTF-8 byte ascending with duplicates rejected

no_change.condition: requested immutable commit already equals the validated visible commit and every compatible version input matches

full_workspace_analysis: rename represented as delete plus add
partial_analysis: modified already-mapped non-root Rust source with stable repository, path, source, crate, module, and versions
inventory_only: inventory change with no extraction or mapping input change
no_change: exact requested commit already visible with matching versions

determinism.replay: 50 sequential repetitions plus 10 shuffled parallel schedules are canonical-byte-identical
determinism.randomized_sequences: incremental target semantic bytes equal clean target semantic bytes after every supported edit

tests.oracle: The CLI refreshes A to B, emits the exact report, atomically advances the head once, and does not execute untrusted code.
Incremental target snapshot, graph, chunks, document projection, and generated Markdown bytes equal an independent clean target result.
The exact reviewed invalidated, added, removed, retained-count, cache, chunk, document, and empty federation-link sets are emitted.
Every maximum-compatible version change selects the exact full rebuild reason and incompatible cache bytes are never reused.
Only the changed source is parsed; exact unchanged cache entries are reused and contain no revision-bound public identities.
Success and every fixed failure validate against closed report or ErrorV7 schemas with exact stream and exit behavior.
Every failpoint exposes the complete baseline or complete target; concurrent movement fails with no partial head.
Git, Cargo, rustc, build, target, hook, plugin, network, model, and Council sentinels remain untouched.
Supported randomized edit and schedule sequences preserve exact cold equivalence, ordering, cache-key, and head invariants.
The accepted S4 contract bundle and every file it binds remain byte-identical.

forbidden: workflow, policy, agent, architecture, or roadmap files
existing accepted decisions, schemas, fixtures, goldens, or contract bundles
target, build, compiler, package-manager, hook, plugin, network, model, or Council execution
baseline public chunk bytes reused for another target commit
cold scan mislabeled as incremental reuse
stop_conditions: cold equivalence, cache authority, rematerialization, invalidation closure, no-change, or head semantics are ambiguous
a cache hit can cross repository, source ownership, path, blob, extractor, normalization, ontology, extraction contract, semantic profile, dependency rule, or cache-schema boundaries
reused analysis can retain commit-bound public evidence or another public identity
the fixture requires target, build, process, network, plugin, model, or Council execution
an accepted S4 artifact or production, policy, workflow, dependency, architecture, roadmap, benchmark, or release path must change
a fixed limit, typed failure, stream, exit, or report meaning cannot be enforced
the task exceeds the allowed paths or high-risk classification
